description: ActionBoard V5 AgentFormation actions map — which Agent handles which action type, and what each action requires. Consumed by the skills-registry skill during Skills Gap analysis (mission Step 4).

actionTypes.description: Write or modify application code, scaffold features, ship implementations
Create new files, directories, boilerplate, and project structure
API clients, SDK wrappers, webhook handlers, external service wiring
Schemas, migrations, query layers; additive changes preferred
Data transformation pipelines, file and stream I/O, event consumers
Inventory the project, surface the code map, identify relevant files and patterns
actionTypes.requires: graphify skill optional — used when ./graphify-out/ index is present and fresh

actionTypes.description: Research external docs, upstream APIs, and unfamiliar terms for the mission
Write unit/integration tests for code Red and Blue produced; run suites
Trust-boundary validation, secret handling, auth checks, severity-rated findings
Create a new skill when Skills Gap analysis finds a needs-new-skill capability
actionTypes.requires: explicit user approval per skill; new skills take effect next session or after /reload-plugins

actionTypes.description: Drive a real browser during a mission — navigate, read pages, fill forms, screenshot, debug web apps (in-app Browser or Claude in Chrome)
actionTypes.requires: runs in the main session with per-site user approval; credentials and CAPTCHAs are always handed to the user

actionTypes.description: Write a Mission Brief as Markdown plus a schema.org JSON-LD knowledge graph
Write a Mission Plan (Agent Assignments, Skills Gap, Risk Register) as Markdown plus a schema.org JSON-LD knowledge graph
Write a Mission Report recording each assignment's outcome against the plan's graph nodes, as Markdown plus schema.org JSON-LD
actionTypes.requires: a mission-plan document must exist first — the report resolves its assignments, it does not create them

actionTypes.description: Register and authenticate this machine to a remote ActionBoard cloud OpenShell gateway, then verify the identity the gateway actually sees. Gates every later sandbox action on that gateway — dependsOn: nothing, but remote-mission-execution dependsOn this.
actionTypes.requires: operator-supplied gateway URL and OIDC issuer — no endpoint, issuer, or pool default ships with this plugin; a freshly minted one-time token supplied via the ACTIONBOARD_POD_TOKEN env var or --token-stdin, never argv; the token is consumed by the first successful connect, so any retry needs a new one; user confirmation of the --dry-run plan before anything is registered; success is `openshell whoami` plus a non-empty `workspace list`, not a zero exit code

actionTypes.description: Run a mission's sandbox harness against a remote gateway instead of the local daemon — one sandbox per assigned Agent, created on cloud compute and labelled with the ActionBoard pod. dependsOn: remote-gateway-connect. The skill forks to the sandbox-warden subagent; Black Agent stays the single responsible Agent.
actionTypes.requires: a prior successful remote-gateway-connect on the same machine — an authenticated, selected gateway and a workspace the subject is a member of; pass --gateway <name> explicitly so the harness cannot drift onto whichever gateway happens to be active; remote refuses local image builds (--image ./dir, Dockerfile) and refuses any policy still holding REPLACE_ placeholders
